summary.text: Jordan Conley is the Green Party nominee. He is a personal trainer, coach, and teacher who founded the nonprofit Hapa Mana in 2016. He says he is running on universal health care, a housing-first approach to homelessness, and opposition to U.S. military engagement abroad.

paragraphs.text: According to Ballotpedia, Conley graduated from Wayne High School. He lists Burger King at age 14 as his first job and says he worked as a bartender and server before spending the last 16 years as a personal trainer, coach, and teacher.

In a Honolulu Star-Advertiser questionnaire, he listed his current occupation as teacher, coach and fitness trainer, said he has been a group fitness instructor for Hawaii Pacific Health for more than 12 years, and named the Aiea Neighborhood Board as a previous elected office.

Conley says he founded the nonprofit Hapa Mana to integrate communities across income lines through sports and educational enrichment, and that COVID-19 shutdowns ended its in-person groups. The Star-Advertiser questionnaire dates the nonprofit's start to September 2016.
He says he had never wanted to run for office. He ran unopposed in the August 8, 2026 Green Party primary, receiving 368 votes.
